items.stem: A withdraw function sends Ether before it updates the user's balance. Which vulnerability class is this?

options.text: Reentrancy, because an external call occurs before state is settled
options.rationale: Correct: the external call can re-enter before the balance updates.
Events are a logging concern, not this bug.
The core issue is reentrancy, not gas griefing.

items.explanation: Correct: the external call can re-enter before the balance updates.

items.stem: Which TWO practices strengthen a smart-contract audit beyond reading the code once? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Writing invariants and fuzzing them against the contract
options.rationale: Correct: fuzzing invariants surfaces edge cases.

options.text: Reproducing a suspected exploit in a test to confirm severity
options.rationale: Correct: a working proof of concept validates the finding.

options.text: Rating all findings as the same severity to be safe
Skipping tests because the code looks clean
options.rationale: Looking clean is not evidence of safety.

items.explanation: Correct: fuzzing invariants surfaces edge cases.

items.stem: Why can a correct-looking contract still be drained by a flash-loan attack?

options.text: The attack manipulates economic inputs like a price oracle rather than breaking the code logic
options.rationale: Correct: economic manipulation exploits design assumptions, not code bugs.
They do not rely on overflow.

options.text: Correct code is immune to all attacks
options.rationale: Correct code can still have economic flaws.

items.explanation: Correct: economic manipulation exploits design assumptions, not code bugs.
